(buggy), and is fixed by starting the c-search at c=0 (fixed). Use the added tests in statsmodels/stats/tests/test_proportion.py to ensure FAIL on the buggy revision and PASS on the fixed one.

strategy.success_criterion: The test suite specified by -k "sison_glaz_sparse" FAILS on the buggy revision (67ca8f98c1ed) because multinomial_proportions_confint(counts, 0.05, method="sison-glaz") raises Exception: "Couldn't find a value for 'c' ..." for one of the sparse count vectors; the same tests PASS on the fixed revision (PR#9909 result) because the implementation handles the c-search by starting at c=0 and returns valid intervals (and matches the provided R reference array for counts=[1,1,0,0,0,0,0]).
strategy.numerical_probe: N/A (the transition is exception-vs-return and the reference equality check); the probe is that sison-glaz c-search no longer fails for sparse counts.

risks: This bug is primarily triggered by small/sparse multinomial counts where nu(1) can exceed 1-alpha or where the Edgeworth approximation nu(c) is non-monotone/plateaus; if the selected counts do not trigger c-search failure on your machine, the test may not fail on the buggy revision.
The defect transition could depend on exact numpy/scipy numerical behavior; use the pinned numpy==2.0.2 and scipy==1.15.3 versions to maximize likelihood of reproducing.

Platform/toolchain risk: statsmodels may compile extensions (Cython/C extensions) depending on build configuration; ensure editable install builds successfully and uses the same Python (3.11.13) and ABI.

If you cannot build statsmodels from source (needs_build=true), you cannot switch between buggy and fixed commits; in that case, install from wheels may mask the failure or prevent it from changing across revisions.

oracle.reference_source: R MultinomialCI (Sison-Glaz) values encoded in test_confint_multinomial_proportions_sison_glaz_sparse_r_reference via ci_r; the test uses assert_allclose with atol=1e-6
oracle.why: The added regression test directly compares cis to the reference array for counts=[1,1,0,0,0,0,0] with assert_allclose(atol=1e-6), which should fail on buggy code and pass on fixed code.

strategy.fails_on_buggy: On 67ca8f98c1ed, calling multinomial_proportions_confint(counts, 0.05, method="sison-glaz") for at least one of the sparse vectors in test_confint_multinomial_proportions_sison_glaz_sparse raises Exception("Couldn't find a value for 'c' ..."); therefore pytest fails due to the uncaught exception.
strategy.passes_on_fixed: On the PR#9909 fixed revision, the same calls return cis arrays; the sparse interval containment assertions succeed for all four vectors, and for counts=[1,1,0,0,0,0,0] cis matches the embedded R reference ci_r within atol=1e-6 (including zero-cell upper bound 0.9655815875).
